title: gapfinder-lit-digest-leila-2027-06
content:
Purpose: quick personal harvest of papers/blogs from last two weeks, surface concrete experiment hooks for local sandbox, and a short list of questions to bring to the next `kv-cache` sync. Not a polished summary — messy notes, prioritized next steps at the end.

Context hookups (why I care): production inference cost reduction via smarter prefix reuse and eviction. We're investigating hybrid strategies (sparse KV + short dense caches) to keep tail latency low without exploding memory footprint. Also thinking about developer ergonomics for pinning context (user-level sticky contexts).

Papers / posts skimmed
1) "Adaptive KV Sharding for Long Contexts" (arXiv 2027-ish) — notes:
   - key idea: dynamic shard placement per-request based on token-level access frequency; reassign hot keys to local low-latency partitions.
   - tradeoffs: metadata churn vs better hit rates; requires fast rebalancer + heartbeat.
   - interesting perf numbers: 30–45% reduction in average token fetch latency at 1M tokens/session workloads when hot-key skew > 5x.
   - question: how sensitive is rebalancer to bursty access (conversational turn spikes)? need sim.

2) "Latent Prefix Caching" (conference poster + blog) — notes:
   - compress prefixes into shorter learned representations that decode to KV vectors when needed. saves memory but adds decode overhead.
   - decode can be batched; authors claim amortized cost lower than storing full KV for long sessions (>10k tokens).
   - open: quality regression for instruction-following prompts? Might need supervised fine-tune for safety-critical prefixes.

3) "Eviction Policies for Mixed-Length Sessions" (workshop) — notes:
   - simple insight: LRU is suboptimal when sessions interleave long static contexts (docs) and short conversational turns — recommends two-tier eviction (document-tier sticky, ephemeral-tier LRU).
   - propose TTL heuristics informed by route metadata (customer tier, pinned-doc flag).
   - we already have a route metadata field — low-effort experiment: implement TTL toggle for pinned contexts.

4) Engineering blog: "When KV Cache Size Kills Latency" (company blog, anecdotal) — notes:
   - practical: memory pressure causes paging, which is catastrophic at tail. their mitigation: proactive sampling + greedy eviction before hitting OS memory pressure.
   - idea for Redwood: add a soft-memory watermark per-pool that triggers aggressive prefix pruning + metrics alerting.

Quick synthesis / heuristics I like
- Two-tier cache: (1) sticky document shards (pinned by user or route) with higher retention and TTLs; (2) ephemeral shared pool optimized for recent tokens, LRU with fast path eviction.
- Adaptive shard placement only if skew detected: run lightweight estimator (exponential moving average of token accesses) and trigger reassign when hot-key ratio > threshold.
- Latent-prefix decode batched on inference-critical path only when hit count promise > threshold (i.e., only decode if session likely to request those keys again).

Concrete follow-ups (priority order)
1) Simulation harness: generate synthetic sessions mixing long docs + chat turns (parameters: doc lengths 2k–40k, churn rate, share factor). Metric outputs: cache hit rate, avg token latency, tail p95/p99. (owner: me; ETA: 1 week)
2) TTL toggle prototype: route config flag to mark contexts as pinned; eviction policy honors pinned TTL. Ship small feature behind flag on dev pool; measure memory and p99 latency. (owner: Mira; ETA: 2 weeks)
3) Greedy pre-evict + alerting: add soft watermark metric and a pre-evict policy that prunes low-utility prefixes when approaching watermark. Quick A/B on canary. (owner: Platform SRE; blocker: SRE bandwidth)
4) KV rebalancer sim: implement tiny rebalancer in sim to see churn vs latency benefits; focus on thresholding logic only. (owner: Jonas; ETA: 3 weeks)

Notes-to-self / heuristics to capture:
- Keep metadata: for any pinned context record (route_id, user_id, pin_reason, size_bytes). Eviction should consult pin_reason priority.
- Cost tradeoff: latent-prefix decode cost is CPU-bound and batch-friendly; favor for cold long-term archives where memory cost >> CPU.
- Measurement: add per-token fetch histogram (not just request-level) to attribute hot-key skew.

Open questions (to discuss in kv-cache sync)
- What is acceptable decode latency for latent prefixes before user-observed degradation? (empiric: <10ms extra per-token?)
- How often do sessions actually revisit old docs vs append-only streams in customer traffic? Need sampling on hosted API.
- Should pinned contexts be billable differently? economics implications. (ask growth/pricing)

Scratch prompt/experiment idea (for eval harness)
- Generate mixed-session trace: start with document of 20k tokens (public wiki article), then interleave 30 Q/A turns that reference random inserted paragraphs. Measure hit rates when sticky pin enabled vs disabled. Report p99 latency and tokens fetched from remote store.

Quick action list (this doc)
- [ ] Build sim harness skeleton (me)
- [ ] Add route-level TTL toggle flag (Mira)
- [ ] Submit tiny telemetry PR for per-token fetch histograms (Jonas)
- [ ] Prep short slide for kv-cache sync summarizing two-tier idea + sim plan (me; due next Tue)

Random scribbles / half-ideas
- Could we use cheap approximate membership (bloom-ish) per-shard to avoid full metadata fetch when checking for potential hits? Might reduce remote tax.
- If we implement latent-prefix, need a mode where decode is incremental (first decode prefix head to check quality) — avoid full decode always.

End notes: keep this lightweight. Pull in snippets to Confluence once sim outputs are ready. Bring the TTL toggle idea as the minimum viable experiment to reduce memory tail events.

References to glance back at:
- arXiv:2303.12736 (adaptive routing/sharding inspiration)
- GitHub PR: redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments#42 (old prototype, re-check metrics)
- CONFLUENCE-ENG-2345 (kv-cache design notes)

-- Leila
